title: Blenda: Dynamically-Reconfigurable Stacked DRAM
problem: Die-stacked DRAMs are typically configured uniformly as either memory or cache, but different workloads have varying memory-cache requirements that change dynamically during application execution phases.
motivation: Die-stacked DRAM is critical for addressing memory bandwidth bottlenecks in modern processors, so optimizing its utilization directly improves system performance.
method: Blenda dynamically partitions stacked DRAM into a memory part that efficiently stores hot data objects and a cache part that captures transient data and filters requests to off-chip DRAM. The system adjusts configurations transparently based on workload phases without reboots, implementing graceful transitions between configurations that minimize data invalidation.
key_novelty: Dynamic workload-aware partitioning of stacked DRAM between memory and cache functions with graceful transitions that eliminate data invalidation.
contributions: Workload-aware dynamic partitioning of stacked DRAM capacity
Reactive configuration adjustment based on application phases without reboots or user involvement
Graceful transitions between configurations that avoid data invalidation
34% performance improvement over prior best-performing architecture with minimal overhead

metrics.other: less than 100 bytes per core overhead
